summary:
You dear, nice chick, sending me such a sweet picture, and the letter—I can’t tell you (well, here I go anyhow) how much it means to me. I’ve got the pic­ ture propped up here right beside my typewriter here on my desk, in my office. 
Farout. Here’s a big kiss back. Thank you, Sue. Bless your heart. And you’re pretty, too. 

You know, Sue, I’ve been vacillating around, trying to get it all together as to (one) staying here in Vancouver or (two) flying down to Fullerton to be with you guys, and this letter and picture from you just about decides it for me. I really sense your warmth, and when you and Will were in San Rafael I dug you both very much. I’m doing a lot better now; the ache inside me has virtually dimmed out, due mainly to the people I’ve been living with here at X-Kalay. The furies are no longer driving me. In leaving here I wouldn’t feel I’d left having failed to get into a productive life here, or that I couldn’t stand it or relate to the people or anything, but simply that Fullerton and you guys offered me more. It would be one positive thing versus another. I’d rather be with you. It’s as basic as that. I want to come to Fullerton, rather, now, than having to. The obsessive, past-haunted drive is out of me. I heard, by the way, from Kathy—nothing more dire has happened to her than that she got fired from her job and is now work­ ing for Safeway. Evidently many of my morbid terrors and apprehensions about her were wasted. I hope so. Of course, if anything were ...
